PRINCIPLE: Test should focus on a single behavior. RATIONALE: Single Arrange-Act-Assert aids root-cause detection. DECISION: Only one distinct method call is exercised and the assertions relate to that action. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests must not depend on others. RATIONALE: Enables parallel and order-independent execution. EVALUATION: The test uses only local variables and does not reference or modify shared static/instance state; no test ordering hints. DECISION: No shared mutable state seen and no setup/teardown required. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows

EVALUATION: The method exercises only a normal path (valid array and k) and contains no exception tests (no assertThrows, no @Test(expected=...), no try/catch verifying error cases). DECISION: There is only one happy-path test and no evidence of an error-case within this test. VERDICT: non-compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should validate boundary inputs. RATIONALE: Boundaries reveal off-by-one bugs. EVALUATION: The test exercises a typical case (array length 6, k=2) and does not include boundary values like k=0, k=length-1, negative k, or empty arrays. DECISION: No boundary test data is present. VERDICT: non-compliant.

EVALUATION: The test contains setup inline (array creation and item insertion) with no helper methods or constants to encapsulate repeated setup. DECISION: No private helper methods or constants exist in the method to eliminate duplication; despite being a single test, the class does not demonstrate modularization. VERDICT: non-compliant.
